title: Social Media Dynamics
body:
A recommendation algorithm scored on engagement will amplify whatever holds attention. That is
the mechanism behind most of what this block covers, and it requires no bad intent from
anybody, which is what makes it hard to fix.

Engagement is measurable: time on the platform, clicks, shares, replies. Content that provokes
a strong reaction produces more of all four than content that informs calmly. A system
optimised on the measurable proxy therefore promotes provocation, and the people who built it
chose the proxy because it was measurable, and the outcome followed without anybody wanting it.
That is the same failure [[ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE]] describes when a reward function is
optimised literally: the system maximises the sentence that was actually written.

The consequences the course covers:

```
sorting            people see different information environments, shaped by what
                   they previously engaged with, and never by what is true
amplification      the most reactive version of a story travels furthest
metrics on approval  attaching a public number to social approval changes how
                   people behave to obtain it
speed              a claim spreads before any correction can be produced
```

The design responses are all trade-offs. Ranking by recency removes the amplification and
floods the user. Human moderation scales poorly and applies inconsistently. Automated
moderation is a [[Classification]] problem with the [[False Positive]] and
[[False Negative]] trade from [[MACHINE LEARNING]], where one error silences
legitimate speech and the other leaves harm in place, and no threshold avoids both.
